spec_acceptance_criteria.description: WaitlistService keeps ProcessCancelledAppointmentAsync (endpoint-called) but no IHostedService
TreatmentLifecycleService keeps StartLifecycleAsync + HandleComplaintEscalationAsync but no IHostedService

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Service classes retained (Singleton) but IHostedService / Timer / Interlocked / StopAsync stripped
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: WaitlistService.ProcessCancelledAppointmentAsync is called fire-and-forget from /cancel endpoint; TreatmentLifecycleService.StartLifecycleAsync + HandleComplaintEscalationAsync are endpoint-invoked. These members must remain DI-injectable. Only scheduling concern migrates to Hangfire.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: Services still exist under new role (endpoint helpers). Only tick/timer plumbing removed.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: WaitlistJob / TreatmentLifecycleJob are thin delegators that call service.ExpireWaitlistEntriesAsync() / service.ProcessDueStepsAsync()
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Keeps helper methods (SendStepMessageAsync, HandleLastStepAsync, SendEscalationAlertAsync, ResolveTemplate) inside the service class where they are shared with endpoint-invoked code paths (HandleComplaintEscalationAsync reuses SendEscalationAlertAsync).
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: Jobs are shells; business logic stays in service. Mirrors Faz 1 pattern where ReminderJob owns all logic because the deleted service had no endpoint callers.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Both jobs share queue=appointments with ReminderJob (Faz 1)
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Same service process, same Hangfire server, same worker pool. Declaring distinct queues per job would fragment concurrency without isolation gain.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: Three recurring jobs (appointments:reminder, appointments:waitlist, appointments:treatment-lifecycle) on queue=appointments.

spec_architectural_decisions.decision: Recurring job id convention: appointments:waitlist, appointments:treatment-lifecycle
spec_architectural_decisions.reason: Matches Faz 1 naming (service:job). Safe idempotent AddOrUpdate per startup.
spec_architectural_decisions.codex_note: EXPECTED: No collision with Faz 1 reminder id.

verification_questions.question: After stripping IHostedService from WaitlistService, does ProcessCancelledAppointmentAsync remain callable from the /cancel endpoint (same DI lifetime = Singleton)?
Does TreatmentLifecycleService.ProcessDueStepsAsync preserve byte-identical logic from the removed private ProcessDueSteps (batch size, escalation branching, cancel behavior)?
Are recurring job ids (appointments:waitlist, appointments:treatment-lifecycle) distinct from Faz 1 appointments:reminder — and register idempotently on service restart?
Hangfire overlap prevention ([DisableConcurrentExecution]) replaces the Interlocked guard — is the timeout appropriate (>= previous cycle duration) for TreatmentLifecycleJob under large batches?
StopAsync graceful-wait (TreatmentLifecycleService waited up to 30s for in-flight processing) is delegated to Hangfire ShutdownTimeout=30s (set in HangfireSetup). Equivalent?
